names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 23 decembrie, «Sfântul Cuvios Naum», with the rank words left off; the life it links is titled «Sfântul Cuvios Naum al Ohridei».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 23 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιος Ναούμ ο Θεοφόρος και θαυματουργός», with the rank word and the two by-names left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 20. јун ст. ст., „Преподобни Наум Охридски“ — Преподобни is the rank and comes off, and Охридски is **kept**, being the by-name the heading itself gives and the thing that distinguishes him rather than grades him. Both forms were measured before the choice: `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Наум Охридски», and for the bare «Наум» it returns `naum-of-aglomazovo`, which holds that string as `ru`. So the fuller form was taken on §6’s rule — the fullest the calendar gives, and bare of rank — and it happens also to be the form that leaves the one other Naum alone.

attestations.note: The life page `/3311/` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 23 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps for the Romanian, and it is the same man: the fellow worker of Cyril and Methodius in Bulgaria whom the Greek calls Θεοφόρος and θαυματουργός. **No `dates` key is drafted.** The folder holds 830 to 23 December 910 from doxologia.ro; saint.gr says only «τον 9ο αιώνα (842 μ.Χ.)», which is a date set against the mission of Cyril and Methodius and not against Naum's own years, so there is nothing here to put against what the folder holds. The page adds his journey to Rome to the then Pope Adrian and his preaching in Germany, and ends with «Ο θάνατος τον βρήκε όρθιο» — death found him on his feet. It names no place of relics and no coordinate is proposed. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

attestations.note:
The day’s third entry, and **the first entry of this wave that names its own principal day and calls the day read a second one**. „Главни му је празник 23. децембра, а 20. јуна му је летњи празник“ — his principal feast is 23 December, and 20 June is his summer feast. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. **THE ROW GOES ON 20 JUNE, THE DAY OF THE PAGE READ, AND THE PRINCIPAL DAY IS WRITTEN NOWHERE AS A FEAST.** §4 forbids moving a principal day under `replace_venerated`, and nothing of the kind is attempted: the `serbian` row was `undocumented`, there was no feast to move, and a reader does not write a feast off a sentence about another day’s page. The folder’s Romanian and Greek rows are both **23 December**, which is the principal day this entry names, so the corpus now holds the principal day from two calendars and the summer day from this one, and that is the true state of it. **OPEN FOR THE AUTHOR**: whoever reads the Julian 12-23 page of this same book will find Naum there as well, and will then be adding a **second** `serbian` feast to a row this day made `venerated` — which is the §4 second-day note working in the direction nobody in this wave has yet had to work it, the principal day arriving after the summer one. It is named here so that it is not discovered as a contradiction. `dates` UNTOUCHED. The folder holds `birth` 830 and `death` 910 off doxologia’s «a trăit între 830 - 23 decembrie 910», and **this entry gives no year of the saint at all**. The one year it prints, 1926, is the year a bell was given to his monastery, a thousand years after him; it is a date in the life of a bell and not of a man, and it is **written in no field**. **WHAT THE ENTRY ACTUALLY IS, AND IT IS NOT A LIFE.** It is an account of the summer feast itself: a great gathering of the people at the monastery of Saint Naum, many sick who come or are carried there to receive healing over the saint’s relics through faith and prayer, and „не само православни него и људи друге вере долазе да потраже помоћ“ — not only the Orthodox but people of another faith come to seek his help. Then one instance, with names: a Muslim of Resen brought and gave the monastery a bell in 1926 out of gratitude that the saint had healed his brother and raised him up again to life from his deathbed; „Прилагач се звао Џемаил Зизо, а његов исцељени брат Сулејман Зизо. Обојица су били угледни грађани у Ресну“ — the donor was called Džemail Zizo and his healed brother Sulejman Zizo, and both were respected citizens of Resen. **Neither man is a folder and neither takes a row**: the object of a wonder is not its subject, and a donor of a bell is not a companion. They are named in the life because they are named in the book, which is the one place in this wave where a wonder has two witnesses with surnames and a date. `types` UNTOUCHED. Преподобни is the `venerable` the folder carries; `monk` and `wonderworker` are there already off the other two books; and **no type is read off this entry at all**, which prints no rank word but that one. No `office`, no `locations` — a monastery named after its founder is not a coordinate, and Resen is the donor’s town and not the saint’s. **NO ROWS.** The entry names no other saint. The folder’s four `related` rows stand untouched, and the new paragraph **deliberately names none of them**, `related-floor` reading a prose name as well as a linked one and this paragraph having no need of any. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S FIFTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Свети Левкије, епископ врунтисиопољски, у Италији“ — Leucius, born in Alexandria, early into a monastery, counted worthy of great revelations and of a mighty grace, so that he raised the dead and drove demons out of men; bishop first in Alexandria, then by a command from heaven crossing into Italy to the pagan city of Vruntisiopolj, which he baptised whole and in which he built a church of the Mother of God; and after much and successful labour passing over into eternity in the time of the emperor Theodosius II, in the fifth century. **Three folders hold the name and not one of them is he.** `ls saints | grep -i leuci` returns exactly three: `leucius-of-caesarea`, a martyr of 249–251 kept with Thyrsus and Coronatus, who is not a bishop and not of Italy; `leucius-companion-of-peter`, a martyr kept with Peter and Severus on the Greek 11 January; and `leucius-of-volokolamsk`, a Russian. `ls saints | grep -iE 'brundis|brindis'` returns nobody at all. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written on this day, and no folder from me — and **the fifth century, Theodosius II and the city are written nowhere**, because there is nothing to write them on. The day’s verse is his, and a verse is not a hymn and not a folder either. THE DAY’S SIXTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Блажени Студије“ — Studius, a notable patrician and consul in Constantinople, who founded near the Golden Gate the church of Saint John the Forerunner and the monastery called the Studion after him; a house that became famous for many glorious men, spiritual fathers, ascetics and sufferers for the faith; destroyed by the Latin crusaders in 1204, restored by the emperor Constantine Palaeologus Porphyrogenitus in 1293, and with a Turkish mosque standing on the place now. `ls saints | grep -i studi` returns five folders and **every one of them is a Studite and not the Studius the house is named after** — `damascene-the-studite`, `james-of-studion`, `naucratius-the-studite`, `nicholas-the-studite`, `theodore-the-studite`. The last of those is the man this entry names as the house’s most famous son, and **he takes no row and no mention in any prose written today**: a founder’s monastery is a dedication and a later inhabitant of it is not a relation. Ruling 3 on Studius himself: named here, no folder from me, and **1204, 1293 and the consulship are written nowhere**. The Блажени of his heading therefore decides nothing, there being no folder for it to decide a type on; had there been one it would still be the §5 reading «fool-for-christ *or* righteous — read which», and a patrician and consul who founds a monastery is neither obviously.

SECOND-DAY NOTE, ADDED 8 OCTOBER 2026 BY THE READER OF THE JULIAN 23 DECEMBER, AND NOTHING ELSE UNDER THIS KEY WAS TOUCHED. The row above is carried back word for word — same day, same month, same source text, same url, same year, and the whole of the reading it came with — under `replace_venerated`, which BRIEF.md §4 sanctions for exactly this and for nothing else. WHAT HAPPENED IS WHAT THE READING ABOVE SAID WOULD HAPPEN. The Охридски пролог for 23. децембар ст. ст., which that reader could only point at, has now been read: `https://www.pravoslavno.rs/index.php?q=citanja&datum=2026-01-05&prolog=1`, the civil 5 January 2026, and its third entry is „Преподобни Наум Чудотворац Охридски.“ over a full life — the disciple of Cyril and Methodius and one of the Петочисленици, the journey to Rome, the knowledge of many languages, the settling on the shores of Lake Ohrid with the help of the emperor Boris Michael, the monastery founded on the southern shore while Clement acted as bishop in Ohrid, the labour of translating the Scriptures and the church books from Greek into Slavonic, and the wonderworking relics that heal grievous sicknesses and madness in particular. SO THE BOOK ITSELF KEEPS HIM ON BOTH DAYS, and its own 20 June entry already told us which it ranks first. THE DAY IS NOT MOVED AND THE SECOND FEAST IS WRITTEN IN NO FIELD: one attestation row per church is the schema, §4 forbids changing the day under this key, and 23 December is recorded here as a note and in the life. He therefore does NOT render on the Serbian 23 December, and the day’s eleven other rows are the ten of Crete and Niphon. OPEN FOR THE AUTHOR, AND NOW WITH BOTH PAGES READ: the corpus keeps this man’s Serbian row on the summer feast while this same book calls 23 December his principal one and prints a life there and an account of a feast here, and the folder’s Romanian and Greek rows are both 23 December. If the row is to stand on the principal day it is the author who moves it, not a reader. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND CONFIRMED RATHER THAN CHANGED: the 23 December entry closes «Упокојио се у првој половини X века», the first half of the tenth century, and the folder’s death of 910 sits inside it, so there is nothing to widen and nothing to choose between. `types` UNTOUCHED: «Преподобни» is the `venerable` and «Чудотворац» the `wonderworker` the folder already carries, and `monk` stands. NO NEW NAME FORM: §6 allows one `sr` form per folder and the folder holds «Наум Охридски», written by the 06-20 reader; this heading gives the fuller «Наум Чудотворац Охридски», and replacing a form another reader measured and wrote — which would empty one fold key and open another — is not a thing this reader will do to a folder on a note. It is named instead. The three saints the new paragraph names, Cyril, Methodius and Clement, ALREADY HOLD `related` ROWS BOTH WAYS on this folder and are linked there; nothing was added. «(в. 20. јун)» closes the entry, pointing back at this very row. The Prologue prints no hymn on 23 December either.

hymns.text:
Ucenic vrednic al Sfinţilor Chiril şi Metodie, te-ai arătat fericite,
Şi tămăduiri din destul ai revărsat cu dragoste sufletelor smerite,
Ca cel ce te-ai arătat luminător mare celor din întunericul neştiinţei,
Cu raza rugăciunii tale ne înconjoară şi pe noi în ceasul umilinţei.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Naum; the page prints the four rhymed lines and no tone

english.text: A worthy disciple of Saints Cyril and Methodius you were shown to be, O blessed one, and healings in plenty you poured out with love upon humble souls; and as one who was shown a great light to those in the darkness of ignorance, surround us also with the ray of your prayer in the hour of our lowliness.
